Module io.github.brantunger.unruly.core
Package io.github.brantunger.unruly.api

Class FactType<T>

java.lang.Object
io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.FactType<T>
Type Parameters:
T - The fact's type: a class, or a parameterized type such as List<String> or Map<String, Applicant>. Its own type arguments can be anything Java allows there, wildcards included
All Implemented Interfaces:
Type
public abstract class FactType<T> extends Object implements Type
A fact's type written with its type arguments, such as List<String>, which a class literal can't say. Create one as an anonymous subclass, which is what keeps the type argument for the engine to read, and declare the fact with it: 

 builder.fact("tags", new FactType<List<String>>() { })

It is a Type, so RulesEngineBuilder.fact(String, Type) and RulesEngineBuilder.facts(java.util.Map<java.lang.String, ? extends java.lang.reflect.Type>) take it as they take a Class or a ParameterizedType from another library. The builder keeps the type it stands for, type(), not the token, so a language is told java.util.List<java.lang.String> as a ParameterizedType, as CompileContext.declaredFacts() describes. A language reads the class of a declared type, whichever kind it is, with CompileContext.rawClass(Type).

Two tokens are equal when the types they stand for are, and a token is never equal to that type itself, a Class or a ParameterizedType, which knows nothing of tokens. It holds no more than the type, so it is immutable and safe to share between threads.
